$(2(j-1)p,2jp]$ contains $p$ even integers, all positive and the largest being $2jp$, so $\Pr(S=2jp)\le\frac1p\Pr(2(j-1)p<S\le2jp)$. Summing
over $j\ge1$ and using symmetry, $\Pr(S\in p\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\})\le\frac2p\Pr(S>0)\le\frac1p$. Finally
$\Pr(S=0)=\binom{2h}h4^{-h}\le(\pi h)^{-1/2}$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:LObases}
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $d\ge1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=*]
\item Let $\varphi\in(\mathbb{F}_p^d)^b$, and suppose that $b$ contains $t\ge2$ pairwise disjoint sets $B_1,\dots,B_t$ with $|B_c|=d$ such that
$(\varphi_j)_{j\in B_c}$ is a basis of $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ for each $c$. Then
$\rho_{\mathbb{F}_p^d}(\varphi)\le\hat\rho_{\mathbb{F}_p^d}(\varphi)\le\big(\frac1p+(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^d$.
\item If every hyperplane of $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ misses at least $k$ of the $\varphi_j$, $j\in b$, then $b$ contains $\lceil k/d\rceil$ pairwise disjoint
sets as in (a).
\item Let $U\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^m$ be a subspace of dimension $d$ such that every nonzero $y\in U$ has $\lvert\operatorname{supp} y\rvert\ge k$, let $\xi$ be uniform in
$\{\pm1\}^m$, and put $t:=\lceil k/d\rceil$. If $t\ge2$, then
\[
\Pr(\bar\xi\perp U)\ \le\ \Big(\frac1p+\big(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor\big)^{-1/2}\Big)^d .
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
(a) Drop the factors with $j\notin B_1\cup\dots\cup B_t$ (each is at most $1$) and apply H\"older's inequality with $t$ factors:
\[
\hat\rho_{\mathbb{F}_p^d}(\varphi)\le\frac1{p^d}\sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{F}_p^d}\prod_{c=1}^t\prod_{j\in B_c}\Bigl|\cos\frac{2\pi\,\tau^{\top}\varphi_j}p\Bigr|
\le\prod_{c=1}^t\Big(\frac1{p^d}\sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{F}_p^d}\prod_{j\in B_c}\Bigl|\cos\frac{2\pi\,\tau^{\top}\varphi_j}p\Bigr|^t\Big)^{1/t}.
\]
For each $c$, $\tau\mapsto(\tau^{\top}\varphi_j)_{j\in B_c}$ is a bijection of $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ onto $\mathbb{F}_p^{B_c}$, as $(\varphi_j)_{j\in B_c}$ is a
basis, so the inner average equals
\[
\Big(\frac1p\sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb{F}_p}\Bigl|\cos\frac{2\pi\sigma}p\Bigr|^t\Big)^d,
\]
which is at most $\big(\frac1p+(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^d$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:LOp}.

(b) Choose the sets greedily. After $c<k/d$ sets of $d$ indices have been removed, every hyperplane still misses at least $k-cd\ge1$ of the
remaining $\varphi_j$. So the remaining vectors lie in no hyperplane and span $\mathbb{F}_p^d$, and there is a set $B_{c+1}$ of $d$ remaining indices
such that $(\varphi_j)_{j\in B_{c+1}}$ is a basis. This works for $c=0,1,\dots,\lceil k/d\rceil-1$.

(c) Let $y^{(1)},\dots,y^{(d)}$ be a basis of $U$ and $\varphi_j:=(y^{(1)}_j,\dots,y^{(d)}_j)\in\mathbb{F}_p^d$ for $j\in[m]$. Then $\bar\xi\perp U$
if and only if $\sum_j\xi_j\varphi_j=0$, and for $a\in\mathbb{F}_p^d\setminus\{0\}$ the number of $j$ with $a^{\top}\varphi_j\ne0$ is
$\lvert\operatorname{supp}\sum_ia_iy^{(i)}\rvert\ge k$, that is, every hyperplane misses at least $k$ of the $\varphi_j$. By (b) and (a),
$\Pr(\bar\xi\perp U)\le\rho_{\mathbb{F}_p^d}(\varphi)\le\big(\frac1p+(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^d$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:seqbases}
Let $p$ be an odd prime, $d\ge1$, $G:=\mathbb{F}_p^d$, and let $W=(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_m)\in G^m$ and $Y\in G^m$ be fixed. Suppose that every
hyperplane of $G$ misses at least $k$ of the $\varphi_j$, and that $t:=\lceil k/d\rceil\ge2$. Let $T$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix
of order $m$, and write $\bar TW=Y$ for the system $\sum_{j=1}^mT_{ij}\varphi_j=Y_i$, $i\in[m]$. Then
\[
\Pr(\bar TW=Y)\ \le\ p^{-dm}\big(1+p(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^{dm}\,e^{1.6d^2p\sqrt t}\,p^{2d^2} .
\]
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:LObases}(b) there are pairwise disjoint sets $B_1,\dots,B_t\subseteq[m]$ with $|B_c|=d$ such that $(\varphi_j)_{j\in B_c}$
is a basis of $G$ for each $c$. In particular $dt\le m$. Order the indices so that $B_t,B_{t-1},\dots,B_1$ come last, in this order, and
apply Lemma~\ref{lem:seqexp}. The rows $1,\dots,m-1$ have suffixes of lengths $m-1,\dots,1$, and a suffix of length $r$ contains
$B_1,\dots,B_{\min(t,\lfloor r/d\rfloor)}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:LObases}(a), and as
$\lfloor\lfloor r/d\rfloor/2\rfloor=\lfloor r/(2d)\rfloor$, the concentration of such a suffix is at most
$\eta_r:=\big(\frac1p+(\pi\lfloor r/(2d)\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^d$ if $2d\le r<dt$, at most
$\eta_\infty:=\big(\frac1p+(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\big)^d$ if $r\ge dt$, and at most $1$ if $r<2d$. Hence
\[
p^{dm}\Pr(\bar TW=Y)\ \le\ (p^d\eta_\infty)^{m-dt}\prod_{2d\le r<dt}\big(p^d\eta_r\big)\cdot p^{2d^2},
\]
where the factor $p^{2d^2}$ accounts for the $2d-1$ rows with suffixes shorter than $2d$ and for the unused last equation. Moreover
$1\le p^d\eta_\infty=(1+p(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2})^d$, so the first factor is at most ${(1+p(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor)^{-1/2})^{dm}}$.
Each value $i=\lfloor r/(2d)\rfloor$ occurs for at most $2d$ values of $r$, and $i<t/2$ when $r<dt$. As
$\sum_{1\le i\le x}i^{-1/2}\le2\sqrt x$ and $1+y\le e^y$,
\[
\prod_{2d\le r<dt}p^d\eta_r\le\exp\Bigl(dp\sum_{2d\le r<dt}\big(\pi\lfloor r/(2d)\rfloor\big)^{-1/2}\Bigr)
\le\exp\Bigl(\frac{2d^2p}{\sqrt\pi}\cdot2\sqrt{t/2}\Bigr)\le e^{1.6d^2p\sqrt t},
\]
because $4/\sqrt{2\pi}<1.6$. Together with the bound for the first factor, this proves the lemma.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:SEplus}
Let $S$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix of order $n$ and $c_1:=10^{-5}$. Let $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SE}}(S)$ be the event that for
every prime $p$ with $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/8}}$, every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ and every $z\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ whose reduction $\bar z$ is nonzero and
satisfies $\bar S\bar z=\lambda\bar z$,
\[
\|z\|^2\ >\ c_1\,n\,p^2 .
\]
Then $\Pr(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SE}}(S))=1-O(2^{-n/8})$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We fix the parameters and check the conditions of Proposition~\ref{lem:blockdelta}.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $\mathcal G$ be the event of
Proposition~\ref{lem:support} for $S$. On $\mathcal G$ every $\bar z$ as in the statement has a support $D$ of size $|D|>n/20$. Fix a
prime $p$ with $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/8}}$ and put
\[
l:=\Big\lceil\frac{100\log p}{\log n}\Big\rceil+1,\quad s:=\lceil n^{0.6}\rceil,\quad
k:=\lceil n^{0.8}\rceil,\quad \delta:=\frac1{100},\quad R^2:=c_1np^2,\quad \sigma:=\frac n{2R^2}=\frac1{2c_1p^2}.
\]
Then $l\le100n^{1/8}/\log n+2$, and for large $n$ we have $s<k$ and the conditions~\eqref{eq:scondsdelta} hold with $N=p$, uniformly
in $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/8}}$. The first holds as $16l\log(200p)=O(n^{1/4})$, while $s\ge n^{0.6}$. For the second, take logarithms:
$\frac{l+1}2\log s\ge30\log p+0.6\log n$, while
\[
\log\bigl(3232\sqrt{\pi l}\,p\bigr)+2l\log(1.5l)\ \le\ 26\log p+1000\,\frac{\log p}{\log n}+0.57\log n+O(1),
\]
because $l\le\frac{100\log p}{\log n}+2$, $\log(1.5l)\le\frac18\log n+5$ and $\log\sqrt l\le\frac1{16}\log n+O(1)$. For large $n$
the right side is below $30\log p+0.6\log n$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We bound the probability that a fixed vector is an eigenvector.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$, a set $D\subseteq[n]$ with $|D|>n/20$,
and $h:=\lfloor|D|/k\rfloor$ disjoint blocks $B_1,\dots,B_h\subseteq D$ of size $k$, depending on $D$ only. For large $n$ we have
$n/20>k$, so $h\ge1$. For $\bar z$ with support $D$ let $\rho^*(\bar z):=\min_i\rho_p(\bar z_{B_i})$, attained at a block $B^*$. The last
statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:seqexp}, with $b=B^*$ and the fixed right side $\lambda\bar z$, gives
$\Pr(\bar S\bar z=\lambda\bar z)\le\rho^*(\bar z)^{n-k}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3.}\ We weight the integer lifts by a discrete Gaussian, which turns the sum over them into an expectation over a random vector
with independent coordinates.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $\theta_0$, $\mu_0$ and $\nu_{\max}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss} for $c=c_1$, so that
$\theta_0\le1.001$ and $\mu_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_1}\,p$. Let
$Y=(Y_j)_{j\in D}$ have independent coordinates with law $\nu(z):=e^{-\sigma z^2}/\mu_0$ on $\mathbb{Z}\setminus p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\bar\nu$ be the
image of $\nu$ on $\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$. Its largest atom $\nu_{\max}$ satisfies $\frac1{p-1}\le\nu_{\max}$ and $\mu_0\nu_{\max}\le1.001$.
Bounding $\mathbf 1\{\|z\|^2\le R^2\}\le e^{\sigma(R^2-\|z\|^2)}$ and summing over the integer lifts,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{Z}^n:\ \|z\|^2\le R^2\\ \operatorname{supp}\bar z=D}}\Pr(\bar S\bar z=\lambda\bar z)
&\le e^{\sigma R^2}\sum_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{Z}^n\\ \operatorname{supp}\bar z=D}}e^{-\sigma\|z\|^2}\rho^*(\bar z)^{n-k}
=e^{n/2}\,\theta_0^{\,n-|D|}\mu_0^{|D|}\;\mathbb{E}\big(\rho^*(\bar Y)^{n-k}\big).
\end{aligned}
\]

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4.}\ We split the expectation according to the level of $\rho^*(\bar Y)$.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Put $\rho_a:=2^a(1+\delta)/p$ for the integers $a\ge0$ with
$\rho_a\le1$. There are at most $2n^{1/8}$ of them. Either $\rho^*(\bar Y)<(1+\delta)/p$, or $\rho^*(\bar Y)\in[\rho_a,2\rho_a)$ for one
of them. The blocks are disjoint, so the vectors $\bar Y_{B_i}$ are independent, and Proposition~\ref{lem:blockdelta}(b) (with $N=p$,
the law $\bar\nu$ and $\rho_0=\rho_a\ge(1+\delta)/p$) gives
\[
\Pr\bigl(\rho^*(\bar Y)\ge\rho_a\bigr)\le\min\bigl(1,\zeta/\rho_a\bigr)^{h(k-s)},\qquad
\zeta:=\frac{6464\sqrt{\pi l}\,\nu_{\max}}{\sqrt s},
\]
where $h(k-s)\ge(|D|/k-1)(k-s)\ge|D|(1-\frac sk)-k$. For large $n$ we have $\zeta\le1$, and with
$M':=\min(n-k,h(k-s))\ge|D|(1-\frac sk)-k$ we get
\[
(2\rho_a)^{n-k}\min\bigl(1,\zeta/\rho_a\bigr)^{h(k-s)}\le2^n\zeta^{M'}\rho_a^{n-k-M'}\le
2^n\zeta^{|D|(1-s/k)-k}.
\]
Now $\mu_0\zeta\le\gamma:=6471\sqrt{\pi l/s}$ and
$\zeta^{-1}\le\sqrt s\,(p-1)/(6464\sqrt{\pi l})\le\sqrt s\,p$, so
\[
\mu_0^{|D|}(2\rho_a)^{n-k}\Pr\bigl(\rho^*(\bar Y)\ge\rho_a\bigr)\le2^n\gamma^{|D|}
(\sqrt s\,p)^{s|D|/k+k}\le2^n\gamma^{n/20}(\sqrt s\,p)^{3n^{0.8}},
\]
using $\gamma<1$ (for large $n$), $|D|>n/20$ and $sn/k+k\le3n^{0.8}$. For the lowest level, as
$\mu_0/p\le\sqrt{2\pi c_1}$,
\[
\mu_0^{|D|}\Big(\frac{1+\delta}p\Big)^{n-k}\le1.01^n(\mu_0/p)^{|D|}p^{-(n-|D|)}p^k\le
\big(1.01\big(\tfrac1p+\sqrt{2\pi c_1}\big)\big)^np^k .
\]

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 5.}\ We sum over $\lambda$, $D$, the levels and the primes, and conclude the proof.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Since
$\mathbb{E}(\rho^*(\bar Y)^{n-k})\le((1+\delta)/p)^{n-k}+\sum_a(2\rho_a)^{n-k}\Pr(\rho^*(\bar Y)\ge\rho_a)$ and
$\theta_0^{n-|D|}\le1.001^n$, the last two displays bound the sum over integer lifts for fixed $\lambda$ and $D$. Summing over the at
most $p$ values of $\lambda$, the $2^n$ sets $D$ and the at most $2n^{1/8}$ levels, the probability that some $\bar z$ with
$\lvert\operatorname{supp}\bar z\rvert>n/20$ and an integer lift of squared norm at most $R^2$ satisfies $\bar S\bar z=\lambda\bar z$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$
is at most
\[
p^{k+1}\big(2.02\sqrt e\cdot1.001\,(\tfrac1{23}+\sqrt{2\pi c_1})\big)^n
+2n^{1/8}p\,(4\sqrt e\cdot1.001)^n\gamma^{n/20}(\sqrt s\,p)^{3n^{0.8}}.
\]
Here $2.02\sqrt e\cdot1.001(\frac1{23}+\sqrt{2\pi c_1})<0.18$ and $p^{k+1}\le e^{2n^{0.925}}$, so the first term is at most
$e^{-1.7n+2n^{0.925}}$. In the second, $l=O(n^{1/8})$ gives $\gamma=O(n^{1/16-0.3})$, so
$\gamma^{n/20}\le e^{-0.0118\,n\log n+O(n)}$, while the other factors are $e^{O(n)}$ and $e^{O(n^{0.93})}$. Summing over the primes
$p\le e^{n^{1/8}}$ and adding $\Pr(\mathcal G^c)=O(2^{-n/8})$ gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:ACplus}
On the event $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SE}}(S)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus}, which has probability $1-O(2^{-n/8})$ for large $n$, we
have, for every prime $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/8}}$ and every eigenvector $w\in\mathbb{F}_p^n$ of $\bar S$ with eigenvalue in $\mathbb{F}_p$,
\[
\rho_p(w)\ \le\ \frac1p+e^{-2c_1n}.
\]
In particular $\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}w=0)\le\frac1p+e^{-2c_1n}$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
For $c\in\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ the dilate $cw$ is an eigenvector with the same eigenvalue, and its lift $\widetilde{cw}$ is a vector $z$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus}. So
$\mu(w)>c_1np^2$ on $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SE}}(S)$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:dilates} gives
$\rho_p(w)\le\frac1p+e^{-2\mu(w)/p^2}<\frac1p+e^{-2c_1n}$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:pencilsupp}
Let $\tau':=\frac1{100}$, and let $T$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix of order $m$. For all sufficiently large $m$, with
probability at least $1-e^{-m}$ over $T$ the following holds for all $U\subseteq[m]$ with $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$, all primes
$23\le p\le e^{m^{1/8}}$, all monic $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree $2$ such that $Q(\bar T)$ is invertible, all nonzero $P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of
degree at most $1$, and all $R\subseteq U^c$ with $|U^c\setminus R|\le\tau'm$: the matrix $C:=P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}$ satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank} C_{R,U}\ \ge\ 0.13m .
\]
Consequently, for such $T$, $U$, $p$ and $Q$, and for $u$ with support $U$ and independent uniform signs on $U$,
\begin{multline*}
\Pr_u\bigl(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)\cap U^c\rvert<\tau'm\ \text{for some nonzero }P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]\text{ with }\deg P\le1\bigr)\\
\le\ p^2\,2^{-0.05m}.
\end{multline*}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We replace $C_{R,U}$ by a matrix $K$ that has the same nullity and does not involve $Q(\bar T)^{-1}$.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Put
$\delta:=\tau'=\frac1{100}$. Fix $U$, $p$, $Q$, $P$ and $R$ as in the statement, write $Q=x^2+b_1x+b_0$ and $P=a_1x+a_0$, and note that
$U\subseteq R^c$. We identify $\mathbb{F}_p^U$ and $\mathbb{F}_p^{R^c}$ with the spaces of the vectors of $\mathbb{F}_p^m$ supported in $U$ and in $R^c$. If
$Q(\bar T)$ is invertible, $u'\in\mathbb{F}_p^U$ and $(Cu')_R=0$, then $y':=Cu'$ lies in $\mathbb{F}_p^{R^c}$ and satisfies
$Q(\bar T)y'=P(\bar T)u'$. Conversely, such a pair $(y',u')$ gives $Cu'=y'$. So the nullity of $C_{R,U}$ equals that of the
$m\times(|R^c|+|U|)$ matrix
\[
K:=\big[\,Q(\bar T)_{\cdot,R^c}\ \big|\ {-P(\bar T)_{\cdot,U}}\,\big],
\]
and $\operatorname{rank} C_{R,U}=\operatorname{rank} K-|R^c|$. For a row vector of length $|R^c|+|U|$, such as a row of $K$, we call its last $|U|$ entries its
\emph{$U$-part}. The matrix $K$ is defined for every $T$, and we show that $\operatorname{rank} K\ge|R^c|+0.13m$ for all choices as above, outside
an event of probability at most $e^{-m}$. Invertibility of $Q(\bar T)$ is used only in this deterministic step.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We decouple by conditioning on all entries of $T$ outside one off-diagonal block, in the spirit of Costello--Tao--Vu
(2006)~\cite{CTV06}.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Choose disjoint $V_1,V_2\subseteq R$ with $|V_1|=|V_2|=\lfloor|R|/2\rfloor$, depending only on $R$, and
condition on all entries of $T$ except the block $T_{V_1,V_2}$ (and its transpose). The entries of this block and of its transpose have
both indices in $V_1\cup V_2\subseteq R$. Every term $\bar T_{il}\bar T_{lj}$ of $(\bar T^2)_{U,R^c}$ has $i,j\in R^c$, so that each of
its two factors has an index in $R^c$, and the entries of $\bar T_{U,R^c}$ and of $P(\bar T)_{U,U}$ have both indices in $R^c$. So the
rows $K_U$ do not involve $T_{V_1,V_2}$. For $i\in V_1$, splitting the sum over
$l$ according to $l\in V_2$ or not, $Q(\bar T)_{i,R^c}=\bar T_{i,V_2}W+f_i$ with $W:=\bar T_{V_2,R^c}$ and $f_i$ fixed (note that
$\bar T_{i,R^c}$ is fixed and $I_{i,R^c}=0$), while $P(\bar T)_{i,U}=a_1\bar T_{i,U}$ is fixed. So the rows $K_i$, $i\in V_1$, are
$\bar T_{i,V_2}[\,W\,|\,0\,]+h_i$ with $h_i$ fixed, and the vectors $T_{i,V_2}$, $i\in V_1$, are independent and uniform in
$\{\pm1\}^{V_2}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3.}\ We bound the probability that a new row fails to raise the rank.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $r_P$ be the corank of
$P(\bar T)_{U,U}=a_1\bar T_{U,U}+a_0I$. Then $\operatorname{rank} K_U\ge|U|-r_P$, and the vectors with zero $U$-part in the span of $K_U$ and of $g$
further rows form a space of dimension at most $r_P+g$ (the $U$-parts of the rows of $K_U$ are the rows of $-P(\bar T)_{U,U}$). Add
the rows $K_i$, $i\in V_1$, one at a time, and let $g$ be the number of them that have raised the rank so far. The vectors
$v[\,W\,|\,0\,]$, $v\in\mathbb{F}_p^{V_2}$, have zero $U$-part, so the next row $K_i$ fails to raise the rank only if $v=\bar T_{i,V_2}$ lies
in a translate of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_p^{V_2}$ of dimension at most $(|V_2|-\operatorname{rank} W)+r_P+g$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:odlyzko}, given the rows
added before, this has conditional probability at most $2^{r_P+g-\operatorname{rank} W}$. If $a_1=0$, then $a_0\ne0$ and $r_P=0$. If $a_1\ne0$, then
$r_P=\operatorname{corank}(\bar T_{U,U}-\vartheta I)$ with $\vartheta:=-a_0/a_1\in\mathbb{F}_p$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4.}\ We show that $W$ has almost full rank and that $r_P$ is small, outside very unlikely events.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces The matrix $W$ has independent
sign entries, and $|R^c|\ge|U|\ge|V_2|$. Exposing its rows one at a time, each fails to raise the rank with probability at most
$2^{-\delta m}$ while the rank is below $|V_2|-\delta m$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:odlyzko}). So $\operatorname{rank} W\ge|V_2|-\delta m$ except
with probability at most $2^m2^{-\delta^2m^2}$. Next, for a fixed $\vartheta\in\mathbb{F}_p$ and a fixed set $U$, the matrix $T_{U,U}$ is a
uniformly random Seidel matrix of order $|U|$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:apriori} the corank of $\bar T_{U,U}-\vartheta I$ exceeds $\delta m$
with probability at most $30\cdot2^{-\delta^2m^2/4}$. With probability $1-e^{-\Omega(m^2)}$, therefore, $\operatorname{rank} W\ge|V_2|-\delta m$
and $r_P\le\delta m$ for all $P$. Here the union bound over $\vartheta\in\mathbb{F}_p$, the sets $U$ and $R$, and $p$ costs $e^{O(m)}$, and
these events involve neither $T_{V_1,V_2}$ nor $Q$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 5.}\ We count the rows that raise the rank and conclude the proof of the rank bound.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces On these events, while $g<\operatorname{rank} W-r_P-\delta m$
each row fails with probability at most $2^{-\delta m}$. So at the end
$g\ge\min(|V_1|,\operatorname{rank} W-r_P-\delta m)-\delta m\ge|V_2|-3\delta m-r_P$, except with probability at most
$2^m2^{-\delta^2m^2}$. Then, as $|R^c|-|U|=|U^c\setminus R|\le\tau'm$,
\[
\operatorname{rank} K-|R^c|\ge|U|-r_P+g-|R^c|\ge g-r_P-\tau'm\ge|V_2|-5\delta m-\tau'm\ge0.13m,
\]
as $|R|\ge0.39m$ and so $|V_2|\ge(0.39m-1)/2$. Union bounds over the $e^{O(m)}$ choices of $U$, $p$, $Q$, $P$ and $R$ give the first
claim.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 6.}\ We deduce the second claim from the rank bound and Odlyzko's lemma.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Suppose that $\lvert\operatorname{supp}(Cu)\cap U^c\rvert<\tau'm$ for some $P$, where
$C=P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}$. Then $R:=U^c\setminus\operatorname{supp}(Cu)$ satisfies $|U^c\setminus R|<\tau'm$ and $(Cu)_R=0$. For fixed $P$ and $R$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:odlyzko} gives $\Pr_u({(Cu)_R=0})\le2^{-\operatorname{rank} C_{R,U}}\le2^{-0.13m}$, as $(Cu)_R=C_{R,U}u_U$. The support of $Cu$ does not
change if $P$ is multiplied by a nonzero scalar, so it suffices to consider at most $p+1\le p^2$ polynomials $P$. With $N:=|U^c|$, which
lies in $[0.4m,0.6m]$, there are at most $\sum_{j\le\tau'm}\binom Nj\le2^{NH(\tau'm/N)}\le2^{0.6H(1/60)m}\le2^{0.074m}$ sets $R$, as
$\tau'm\le N/2$ and $NH(\tau'm/N)$ increases with $N$. So the probability is at most $p^2\,2^{0.074m-0.13m}\le p^2\,2^{-0.05m}$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:Ptrue}
Let $T$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix of order $m$, $c_2:=e^{-1500}$, and let $u$, $U$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:squaring}. For
all sufficiently large $m$, with probability at least $1-e^{-m/200}$ over $T$ the following holds for every prime
$23\le p\le e^{m^{1/8}}$ and every monic $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree $2$ such that $Q(\bar T)$ is invertible:
\[
\Pr_u\Bigl(\mu\big((P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)_{U^c}\big)\le c_2mp^2\ \text{for some nonzero }P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]\text{ with }\deg P\le1\Bigr)\
\le\ e^{-m/100},
\]
and consequently $|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\,\xi^{\top}P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}\xi/p)|\le e^{-c_2m/2}$ for every nonzero $P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree at
most $1$. In particular, if $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\bar T-\lambda I$ is invertible, then with $B:=(\bar T-\lambda I)^{-1}$, for all
$(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb{F}_p^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$,
\[
\Big|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp\Bigl(\frac{2\pi i\,(t_1\,\xi^{\top}B\xi+t_2\,\xi^{\top}B^2\xi)}p\Bigr)\Big|\ \le\ e^{-c_2m/2}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We fix the parameters and reduce the first claim to a bound for the probability that a linear system for pairs of vectors
has a solution with a short integer lift and a large support.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $(p,Q)$, write $Q=x^2+b_1x+b_0$, and fix a vector
$u\in\{-1,0,1\}^m$ whose support $U$ satisfies $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$. Let $\tau'=\frac1{100}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:pencilsupp}, and put
$m':=|U^c|$, $G:=\mathbb{F}_p^2$, $R^2:=c_2mp^2$, $\sigma:=1/(2c_2p^2)$ (so $\sigma R^2=m/2$), $\delta:=\frac1{100}$, and
\[
l:=\Big\lceil\frac{200\log p}{\log m}\Big\rceil+50,\qquad s:=\lceil m^{0.6}\rceil,\qquad k:=\lceil m^{0.8}\rceil .
\]
For large $m$ these satisfy the conditions of Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd} with $d=2$, uniformly in $23\le p\le e^{m^{1/8}}$. Indeed
$l\ge50$, $s<k$ and $s\ge1400l$. As $2l\log(1.5l)\le\frac14l\log m$ for large $m$, $s^{l/2}(1.5l)^{-2l}\ge m^{0.05l}\ge p^{10}$, which
exceeds both $100p$ and $\frac{32(1+\delta)}\delta\sqrt{\pi l}\,p^2s^{-1/2}$ (the latter gives the second condition
in~\eqref{eq:scondsdelta} with $N=p^2$). Finally, $s=\lceil m^{0.6}\rceil$ is much larger than $16l\log(200p^2)$.

If $Q(\bar T)$ is invertible and $\mu((P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)_{U^c})\le R^2$ for some nonzero $P=a_1x+a_0$, then some nonzero
multiple $y$ of $P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u$ is such that $y_{U^c}$ has an integer lift $z$ with $\|z\|^2\le R^2$. With
$v:=Q(\bar T)^{-1}u$ and $v':=\bar Tv$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pairP}
\bar Tv=v',\qquad\bar Tv'=u-b_1v'-b_0v,
\end{equation}
and $y_j=\ell(v_j,v'_j)$ for all $j$, where $\ell$ is a nonzero multiple of the linear form $(g_1,g_2)\mapsto a_0g_1+a_1g_2$ on $G$.
Let $\mathcal S$ be the event of Lemma~\ref{lem:pencilsupp} for $T$. It has probability at least $1-e^{-m}$ and does not depend on
$(p,Q)$, and on it, if $Q(\bar T)$ is invertible, then for every $U$ with $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$,
\[
\Pr_u\bigl(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)\cap U^c\rvert<\tau'm\text{ for some nonzero }P\text{ with }\deg P\le1\mid T,U\bigr)\le
p^2\,2^{-0.05m}.
\]
Let $\Psi(u)$ be the probability over $T$ that~\eqref{eq:pairP} holds for some pair $(v,v')$ and some nonzero linear form $\ell$ on $G$
such that the vector $y$ with $y_j=\ell(v_j,v'_j)$ satisfies $\lvert\operatorname{supp} y\cap U^c\rvert\ge\tau'm$ and $y_{U^c}$ has an integer lift of squared
norm at most $R^2$. In Steps~2--4 we show that $\Psi(u)\le e^{-m/2}$ for large $m$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We change coordinates, sort the coordinates into classes and set up the weights.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $\ell$ and an $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear bijection
$\varphi:G\to G$ whose second coordinate is $\ell$, and put $w_j:=\varphi(v_j,v'_j)=(\check v_j,y_j)$. Then~\eqref{eq:pairP} is
equivalent to $\sum_jT_{ij}w_j=\varphi(v'_i,u_i-b_1v'_i-b_0v_i)$ for all $i$, a linear system for $T$ whose right side is determined by
$w$ and $u$. Each coordinate $j$ lies in one of five classes, namely $Z$ ($w_j=0$), $D_1$ ($j\in U$, $y_j\ne0$), $D_2$ ($j\in U^c$,
$y_j\ne0$), $D_3$ ($j\in U$, $y_j=0\ne\check v_j$) and $D_4$ ($j\in U^c$, $y_j=0\ne\check v_j$). For each pattern
$\mathcal D=(D_1,\dots,D_4)$ with $|D_2|\ge\tau'm$ fix disjoint blocks of size $k$, $\lfloor|D_i|/k\rfloor$ of them inside each $D_i$,
depending only on $\mathcal D$. There is at least one, as $|D_2|\ge\tau'm\ge k$. Let $\rho^*(w)$ be the smallest value of $\rho_G$ on
these blocks. Ordering the coordinates so that a block attaining $\rho^*$ comes last, Lemma~\ref{lem:seqexp} (for vectors with entries
in $G$) shows that~\eqref{eq:pairP} has probability at most $\rho^*(w)^{m-k}$ over $T$, the right side being fixed. On $U^c$ we bound
$\mathbf 1\{\|z\|^2\le R^2\}\le e^{\sigma(R^2-\|z\|^2)}$ and sum over the integer lifts $z$ of $y_{U^c}$, while all other coordinates are
counted with weight $1$. Let $\theta_0$ and $\mu_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss} for $c=c_2$ (note $c_2\le10^{-5}$), and let
$\nu^{\rm G}$ be the image on $\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ of the probability law proportional to $e^{-\sigma z^2}$ on $\mathbb{Z}\setminus p\mathbb{Z}$, with largest
atom $\nu^{\rm G}_{\max}$. Then $\theta_0\le1.001$, $\mu_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_2}\,p$ and $\mu_0\nu^{\rm G}_{\max}\le1.001$. The total weight
of a class at one coordinate (its \emph{mass}) and the normalized law $\nu_i$ on $G\setminus\{0\}$ are as follows.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item $D_1$: mass $p(p-1)$, and $\nu_1$ is uniform on $\mathbb{F}_p\times\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$.
\item $D_2$: mass $p\mu_0$, and $\nu_2$ is the product of the uniform law on $\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\nu^{\rm G}$.
\item $D_3$: mass $p-1$, and $\nu_3$ is uniform on $\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}\times\{0\}$.
\item $D_4$: mass $(p-1)\theta_0$, and $\nu_4=\nu_3$.
\item $Z$: mass $1$ on $U$ and $\theta_0$ on $U^c$.
\end{itemize}
Every term also carries the global factor $e^{\sigma R^2}=e^{m/2}$. By the list, $\mathrm{mass}_i\nu_{i,\max}\le1.001$ for every class
$i\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, where $\nu_{i,\max}$ is the largest atom of $\nu_i$. The lines of $G$ are $\{y=0\}$ and the lines
$\{\check v=\alpha y\}$, $\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_p$. Each line $\{\check v=\alpha y\}$ has $\nu_1$- and $\nu_2$-measure $\frac1p$, and $\{y=0\}$
has measure $0$. So the largest measure $\kappa_{1,i}$ of a line under $\nu_i$, which is the quantity $\kappa_1$ of
Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd} for $\nu_i$, is $\frac1p$ for $i=1,2$, while $\kappa_{1,3}=\kappa_{1,4}=1$. Hence
$\mathrm{mass}_i\kappa_{1,i}\le1.001p$ for $i\ne2$, and $\mathrm{mass}_2\kappa_{1,2}=\mu_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_2}\,p$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3.}\ We bound the contribution of the lowest level.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces The total mass at a coordinate is $p^2$ on $U$ and $p(\theta_0+\mu_0)$ on
$U^c$. Summing over the fewer than $p^2$ forms $\ell$ and over all $w$ with $\rho^*(w)<(1+\delta)/p^2$, the contribution is at most
\[
p^2e^{m/2}\,p^{2|U|}\big(p(\theta_0+\mu_0)\big)^{m'}\Big(\frac{1+\delta}{p^2}\Big)^{m-k}\le
p^{2k+2}\Big(e^{1/2}(1+\delta)\big(\tfrac{1.001}{23}+\sqrt{2\pi c_2}\big)^{0.4}\Big)^m\le
p^{2k+2}\,0.51^m .
\]

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4.}\ We bound the contribution of the structured levels.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces For the integers $a\ge0$ with $\rho_a:=2^a(1+\delta)/p^2\le1$, fix a
pattern with $|D_2|\ge\tau'm$ and consider the $w$ with $\rho^*(w)\in[\rho_a,2\rho_a)$. Every block then has
$\hat\rho_G\ge\rho_G\ge\rho_a$, and under the product of the laws $\nu_i$ the blocks are independent. By Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd}
with $d=2$, a block of class $i$ has $\hat\rho_G\ge\rho_a$ with probability at most $\zeta_i^{k-s}$, where
$\zeta_i:=\gamma_{1,i}(\rho_a)+1.1\kappa_{1,i}\mathbf 1\{\rho_a\in W^{(1)}\}$, $\gamma_{1,i}$ is the function $\gamma_1$ of that
proposition for $\nu_i$, and $W^{(1)}\subseteq(0,1.1/p)$ is its window. Let $M_i$ be $k-s$ times the number of blocks in $D_i$, and
$M_{\rm bl}:=\sum_iM_i$. As $p^{-2}\le\rho_a\le1$ and $M_{\rm bl}\le m$, we have $(2\rho_a)^{m-k}\rho_a^{-M_{\rm bl}}\le2^mp^{2k}$. In
each block, $k-s$ of the mass factors are paired with the factor $\zeta_i$ of the block bound and with one factor $\rho_a$ (we call these
the \emph{chain coordinates}, and only their number matters). Since $\sum_i(|D_i|-M_i)\le4k+s\lceil m/k\rceil\le6k$, at most $6k$
coordinates outside $Z$ are not paired, each of mass at most $p^2$. The masses of $Z$ contribute at most $1.001^m$. So the contribution
of the pattern and the level, summed over $\ell$, is at most
\[
p^2\,e^{m/2}\,1.001^m\,p^{12k}\cdot2^mp^{2k}\prod_i\big(\mathrm{mass}_i\,\zeta_i\,\rho_a\big)^{M_i}.
\]
Per chain coordinate of class $i$,
$\mathrm{mass}_i\,\gamma_{1,i}(\rho_a)\,\rho_a=\mathrm{mass}_i\nu_{i,\max}\cdot64(1+\delta)\sqrt{\pi l}/(\delta\sqrt s)\le1.001\gamma_0$
with $\gamma_0:=6464\sqrt{\pi l/s}$, and $1.1\,\mathrm{mass}_i\kappa_{1,i}\rho_a\le1.21\,\mathrm{mass}_i\kappa_{1,i}/p$ when
$\rho_a\in W^{(1)}$. So if $\rho_a\notin W^{(1)}$, every factor is at most $1.001\gamma_0$. If $\rho_a\in W^{(1)}$, the factors are at
most $1.001\gamma_0+1.22\le1.23$ for $i\ne2$ and at most $1.001\gamma_0+1.21\sqrt{2\pi c_2}\le2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_2}$ for $i=2$, once $m$
is so large that $\gamma_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_2}$. As $M_2\ge(k-s)(\tau'm/k-1)\ge\tau'm/2$, the product is at most
$(1.001\gamma_0)^{\tau'm/2}$ in the first case and at most $1.23^m(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_2})^{\tau'm/2}$ in the second. Finally
$p^{14k+2}=e^{O(m^{0.93})}$, there are at most
$3^m$ patterns and at most $3m^{1/8}$ levels, $2\cdot1.001e^{1/2}\cdot3<9.91$ and $2\cdot1.001e^{1/2}\cdot3\cdot1.23<12.2$. Hence, with
the bound of Step~3,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi(u)&\le p^{2k+2}0.51^m+e^{o(m)}\Big(9.91^m(1.001\gamma_0)^{m/200}
+12.2^m\big(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_2}\big)^{m/200}\Big)\\
&\le e^{-m/2}
\end{aligned}
\]
for large $m$. Indeed, the first term is $e^{-0.67m+o(m)}$, in the second $\gamma_0\to0$, and in the third
$2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_2}<e^{-745}$, so that $12.2\,(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_2})^{1/200}<12.2\,e^{-3.7}<e^{-1.1}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 5.}\ We combine the bound on $\Psi(u)$ with Lemma~\ref{lem:pencilsupp} and Markov's inequality, and deduce the claims of the
proposition.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $(p,Q)$, and let $\Phi(T)$ be the probability over $u$ in the statement if $Q(\bar T)$ is invertible, and $\Phi(T):=0$
otherwise. If the event in the statement occurs for $u$, then either ${\lvert\operatorname{supp}(P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)\cap U^c\rvert}<\tau'm$ for the polynomial
$P$ in question, or~\eqref{eq:pairP} holds for a pair counted in $\Psi(u)$ (note that $\operatorname{supp} y=\operatorname{supp}(P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}u)$). As
$|U|$ is the sum of the $m$ independent indicators $\mathbf 1\{u_j\ne0\}$ of mean $\frac12$, Hoeffding's inequality
(1963)~\cite[Theorem~2]{Hoe63} gives $\Pr\bigl(\big||U|-\frac m2\big|>0.1m\bigr)\le2e^{-m/50}$. As $u$ is independent of $T$, this bound,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pencilsupp} and the bound on $\Psi(u)$ give
\[
\mathbb{E}_T\Phi(T)\le2e^{-m/50}+\Pr(\mathcal S^c)+p^2\,2^{-0.05m}+\max_u\Psi(u)\le3e^{-m/50}
\]
for large $m$, the maximum being over the $u$ with $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$. By Markov's inequality, $\Phi(T)>e^{-m/100}$ with
probability at most $3e^{-m/100}$, and a union bound over the at most $e^{3m^{1/8}}$ pairs $(p,Q)$ gives the first claim. For the
second, let $P\ne0$ have degree at most $1$. The matrix $C:=P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}$ is symmetric, as $\bar T$ is, and the first claim
is the hypothesis of the last statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:squaring} for $C$, with $t=1$ and $c=c_2$. That statement gives
$|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\,\xi^{\top}C\xi/p)|\le\sqrt2\,e^{-c_2m}\le e^{-c_2m/2}$ for large $m$. Finally, if $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ and
$\bar T-\lambda I$ is invertible, then $t_1B+t_2B^2=P(\bar T)Q(\bar T)^{-1}$ with $Q:=(x-\lambda)^2$, for which
$Q(\bar T)=(\bar T-\lambda I)^2$ is invertible, and $P:=t_1(x-\lambda)+t_2$, which is nonzero as $(t_1,t_2)\ne(0,0)$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:corank}
Let $p$ be an odd prime, $d\ge1$, $q:=p^d$ with $q\ge23$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $S$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix of order
$n\ge4$, and for $m\le n$ let $S_m$ be its leading principal submatrix of order $m$, $L_m:=\bar S_m-\lambda I$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$,
$K_m:=\ker L_m\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^m$ and $r_m:=\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q}K_m$. For $m<n$ let $\xi\in\{\pm1\}^m$ be the part of column $m+1$ of $S$ above the
diagonal. Let $m_0:=\lceil3n/4\rceil$ and $0\le\varpi\le10^{-5}$, and for $m_0\le m<n$ let $\mathcal E_m$ be an event determined by
$S_m$ on which, conditionally on $S_m$,
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\Pr(r_{m+1}=1)\le q^{-1}+\varpi$ if $r_m=0$, and
\item $\Pr(\bar\xi\perp K_m)\le q^{-r_m}+\varpi$ if $r_m\ge1$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\mathcal E_{<m}:=\bigcap_{m_0\le j<m}\mathcal E_j$, the whole space for $m=m_0$, and let $C_0$ be the constant of
Lemma~\ref{lem:apriori}. Then, for $m_0\le m\le n$,
\[
\Pr\bigl(r_m\ge2;\ \mathcal E_{<m}\bigr)\le\frac{1.2}{q^2}+\varpi+C_0\,0.163^{(m-m_0-1)/2},
\]
and $\Pr(r_n\ge1)\le\frac1q+\frac{1.2}{q^2}+2\varpi+C_0\,0.163^{(n-m_0-2)/2}+\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)$.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We bound the conditional expectation of a potential after one step.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces For $m<n$ we have
\[
L_{m+1}=\begin{pmatrix}L_m&\bar\xi\\ \bar\xi^{\top}&-\lambda\end{pmatrix},
\]
and $\xi$ is uniform and independent of $S_m$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:border}, applied over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $L=L_m$ and $c=-\lambda$, we have
$|r_{m+1}-r_m|\le1$, $r_{m+1}\le1$ if $r_m=0$, and $r_{m+1}\ge r_m$ only if $\bar\xi\perp K_m$. Let $V(r):=10^{r-2}$ for $r\ge2$ and
$V(r):=0$ for $r\in\{0,1\}$, and put $\theta_1:=q^{-1}+\varpi$, $\theta_2:=q^{-2}+\varpi$ and $\kappa:=0.1+10\theta_2$. We show that, for
$m_0\le m<n$, on $\mathcal E_m$
\[
\mathbb{E}\big(V(r_{m+1})\mid S_m\big)\le\theta_1\mathbf 1\{r_m=1\}+\kappa V(r_m),\qquad\Pr(r_{m+1}\ge1\mid S_m)\le\theta_1+\mathbf 1\{r_m\ge2\},
\]
where the second inequality is trivial if $r_m\ge2$. If $r_m=0$, then $V(r_{m+1})=0$, and $\Pr(r_{m+1}\ge1\mid S_m)\le\theta_1$ by (i). If
$r_m=1$, then $V(r_{m+1})=\mathbf 1\{r_{m+1}=2\}$, and both $r_{m+1}=2$ and $r_{m+1}\ge1$ require $\bar\xi\perp K_m$, which has
conditional probability at most $\theta_1$ by (ii). If $r_m=2$, then $V(r_{m+1})\le10\cdot\mathbf 1{\{\bar\xi\perp K_m\}}$, of conditional
expectation at most $10\theta_2\le\kappa V(2)$. If $r_m=r\ge3$, then $V(r_{m+1})\le{V(r-1)+V(r+1)\mathbf 1\{\bar\xi\perp K_m\}}$, of
conditional expectation at most $0.1V(r)+10(q^{-r}+\varpi)V(r)\le\kappa V(r)$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We solve the resulting recursion and deduce both claims.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Put $v_m:=\mathbb{E}(V(r_m);\ \mathcal E_{<m})$ and
$a_m:=\Pr(r_m\ge1;\ \mathcal E_{<m})$. As $\mathcal E_{<m+1}\subseteq\mathcal E_{<m}\cap\mathcal E_m$ is determined by $S_m$, Step~1 and
$\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\le V(r)$ give $v_{m+1}\le\theta_1a_m+\kappa v_m$ and $a_{m+1}\le\theta_1+v_m$ for $m_0\le m<n$. Hence
$v_{m+1}\le\theta_1^2+\theta_1v_{m-1}+\kappa v_m$ for $m_0<m<n$. Lemma~\ref{lem:apriori}, applied to the uniformly random Seidel matrix
$S_m$, for which $g_\lambda(S_m)=r_m$, gives $\mathbb{E}(10^{r_m})\le C_0$, so that $v_{m_0},v_{m_0+1}\le C_0$. Put
$\vartheta:=\theta_1+\kappa=q^{-1}+0.1+10q^{-2}+11\varpi$. As $q\ge23$ and $\varpi\le10^{-5}$, we have $\vartheta\le0.163$. As
$\theta_1^2+\vartheta\,\theta_1^2/(1-\vartheta)=\theta_1^2/(1-\vartheta)$ and $\theta_1+\kappa\sqrt{0.163}\le\vartheta\le0.163$, induction
on $m$, starting from $m\in\{m_0,m_0+1\}$, gives
\[
v_m\le\frac{\theta_1^2}{1-\vartheta}+C_0\,0.163^{(m-m_0-1)/2}\qquad(m_0\le m\le n).
\]
As $\Pr(r_m\ge2;\ \mathcal E_{<m})\le v_m$, $\theta_1^2\le q^{-2}+0.1\varpi$ and $1/(1-\vartheta)\le1.195$, this proves the first claim.
Finally $\Pr(r_n\ge1)\le a_n+\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)\le\theta_1+v_{n-1}+\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)$, which gives the second claim.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:rankp}
Let $S$ be a uniformly random Seidel matrix of order $n$, and for a prime $p$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ let $\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\bar S-\lambda I)$ be
the dimension of the kernel of $\bar S-\lambda I$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$. There is an absolute constant $c_3>0$ such that for all sufficiently large
$n$, every prime $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/9}}$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$,
\[
\Pr\bigl(\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\bar S-\lambda I)\ge2\bigr)\le\frac{1.2}{p^2}+e^{-c_3n},\qquad
\Pr\bigl(\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\bar S-\lambda I)\ge1\bigr)\le\frac1p+\frac{1.2}{p^2}+e^{-c_3n}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
We use the notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} with $d=1$, so that $q=p$, $L_m=\bar S_m-\lambda I$ and
$r_m=\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\bar S_m-\lambda I)$. For $m_0\le m<n$ let $\mathcal E_m$ be the intersection of the events of
Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus} and Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue} for $S_m$. For large $n$ they cover $p$, as $n^{1/9}\le m^{1/8}$ for $m\ge m_0$,
and $\Pr(\mathcal E_m^c)\le O(2^{-m/8})+e^{-m/200}$. Put $\varpi:=e^{-c_2m_0/2}$, so that $\varpi\le10^{-5}$ for large $n$ and
$e^{-2c_1m}\le\varpi$. We check the hypotheses (i) and (ii) of Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} on $\mathcal E_m$, conditionally on $S_m$.

If $r_m=0$, let $B:=L_m^{-1}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:border}, $r_{m+1}=1$ if and only if $\xi^{\top}B\xi=-\lambda$. By Fourier inversion,
$\Pr(\xi^{\top}B\xi=-\lambda)\le\frac1p+\max_{t\ne0}|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\,t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi/p)|$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue}, with
$t_1=t$ and $t_2=0$, bounds the maximum by $e^{-c_2m/2}\le\varpi$, which gives (i).

If $r_m=r\ge1$, then Fourier inversion over $K_m$, that is, $\mathbf 1\{\bar\xi\perp K_m\}=p^{-r}\sum_{v\in K_m}e^{2\pi i\,v^{\top}\xi/p}$,
gives
\[
\Pr(\bar\xi\perp K_m)\le p^{-r}+\max_{0\ne v\in K_m}\prod_j\Bigl|\cos\frac{2\pi v_j}p\Bigr|\le p^{-r}+e^{-2c_1m}\le p^{-r}+\varpi .
\]
This is (ii), since Lemma~\ref{lem:dilates} (with $c=1$) bounds the product by $e^{-2\mu(v)/p^2}$, while $\mu(v)>c_1mp^2$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus}, as every nonzero multiple of $v$ is an eigenvector of $\bar S_m$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$.

So Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} applies, and moreover $\Pr(r_n\ge2)\le\Pr(r_n\ge2;\ \mathcal E_{<n})+\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)$,
$\varpi=e^{-\Omega(n)}$, $n-m_0-2\ge n/4-3$ and $\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)\le\sum_{m_0\le m<n}(O(2^{-m/8})+e^{-m/200})=e^{-\Omega(n)}$. As all
these bounds are uniform in $p$ and $\lambda$, both claims follow for a suitable absolute constant $c_3>0$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:isocond}
There is an absolute constant $c_4>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ and every prime $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/9}}$, a uniformly
random Seidel matrix $S$ of order $n$ satisfies
\[
\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p}\Pr\bigl(\lambda\text{ is a repeated root of }\chi_S\bmod p\bigr)\ \le\ \frac{3.5}p+e^{-c_4n},
\]
that is, the expected number of repeated roots of $\chi_S$ modulo $p$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ is at most $\frac{3.5}p+e^{-c_4n}$.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We set up the exposure and record the transitions.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $S_m$, $L_m$, $r_m$, $K_m$, $\xi$, $m_0$,
$\mathcal E_m$, $\mathcal E_{<m}$ and $\varpi$ be as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:rankp}. When $r_m=1$ let $\iota_m:=1$ if the
kernel vectors $w$ of $L_m$ satisfy $w^{\top}w=0$, and $\iota_m:=0$ otherwise. By Lemma~\ref{lem:simple}(d), $\lambda$ is a repeated
root of $\chi_{S_m}$ modulo $p$ if and only if $r_m\ge2$, or $r_m=1$ and $\iota_m=1$. For $m_0\le m<n$, the following holds on
$\mathcal E_m$, conditionally on $S_m$.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item If $r_m=0$, let $B:=L_m^{-1}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:border} (with $L=L_m$ and $c=-\lambda$), $r_{m+1}=1$ if and only if
$\xi^{\top}B\xi=-\lambda$, and then $K_{m+1}$ is spanned by $(B\xi,-1)$, so $\iota_{m+1}=1$ if and only if moreover $\xi^{\top}B^2\xi=-1$.
By Fourier inversion in two variables and Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue},
\[
\Pr(r_{m+1}=1,\ \iota_{m+1}=1)\le\frac1{p^2}+\max_{(t_1,t_2)\ne(0,0)}
\Big|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp\Bigl(\frac{2\pi i\,(t_1\xi^{\top}B\xi+t_2\xi^{\top}B^2\xi)}p\Bigr)\Big|\le\frac1{p^2}+\varpi .
\]
\item If $r_m=1$ and $r_{m+1}=1$, then $\bar\xi\perp K_m$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:border}(b) shows that $K_{m+1}=K_m\times\{0\}$, so that
$\iota_{m+1}=\iota_m$. Hence $\Pr(r_{m+1}=1,\ \iota_{m+1}=1)\le\iota_m\Pr(\bar\xi\perp K_m)\le\iota_m(\frac1p+\varpi)$, by (ii) in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:rankp}.
\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We solve the resulting recursion and sum over $\lambda$.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $d_m:=\Pr(r_m=1,\ \iota_m=1;\ \mathcal E_{<m})$. As
$\mathcal E_{<m+1}\subseteq\mathcal E_{<m}\cap\mathcal E_m$ is determined by $S_m$, Step~1 gives
\[
d_{m+1}\le p^{-2}+\varpi+\Big(\frac1p+\varpi\Big)d_m+\Pr(r_m\ge2;\ \mathcal E_{<m})\qquad(m_0\le m<n),
\]
and by Lemma~\ref{lem:corank}, $\Pr(r_m\ge2;\ \mathcal E_{<m})\le1.2p^{-2}+\omega_n$ for $m\ge m_1:=m_0+\lceil n/8\rceil$, where
$\omega_n:=\varpi+C_0\,0.163^{n/16-1}$. Iterating from $m_1$, where $d_{m_1}\le1$, we get
\[
d_n\le\frac{2.2p^{-2}+\varpi+\omega_n}{1-\frac1p-\varpi}+\Big(\frac1p+\varpi\Big)^{n-m_1}\le2.3\,p^{-2}+e^{-\Omega(n)},
\]
as $2.2/(1-\frac1p)\le2.3$ for $p\ge23$, while $\varpi$, $\omega_n$ and $(\frac1p+\varpi)^{n-m_1}\le0.05^{n/8-2}$ are $e^{-\Omega(n)}$.
Hence, by Theorem~\ref{thm:rankp},
\[
\Pr\bigl(\lambda\text{ is a repeated root of }\chi_S\bmod p\bigr)\le\Pr(r_n\ge2)+d_n+\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)\le3.5\,p^{-2}+e^{-\Omega(n)}.
\]
All the error terms are uniform in $p$ and $\lambda$, and summing over the $p\le e^{n^{1/9}}$ values of $\lambda$ gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:deg1}
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)$. Then the probability that $E_p^{(1)}$ holds for some odd prime $p$ with
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ tends to $0$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Let $\Pi_n:=\{(p,1):\ p\text{ prime},\ n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}\}$, and let $n$ be so large that
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\ge23$ and $n^{1/10}\le(n-1)^{1/9}$. Then every prime $p$ with $(p,1)\in\Pi_n$ is odd and satisfies
$23\le p\le e^{m^{1/9}}\le e^{m^{1/8}}$ for $m\in\{n-1,n\}$. For $m\in\{n-1,n\}$ let $\mathcal G_m$ be the set of Seidel matrices $T$ of
order $m$ for which the event $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{SE}}(T)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus} holds. We verify the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction}, which then proves the proposition. Let $m\in\{n-1,n\}$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:SEplus},
$\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G_m)=O(2^{-m/8})\to0$. Fix a prime $p$ with $(p,1)\in\Pi_n$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that $\beta=x-\lambda$ is a
repeated factor of $S_m$ at $p$. If $S_m\in\mathcal G_m$, Corollary~\ref{cor:ACplus} (for $S_m$) gives
$\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}w=0)\le\frac1p+e^{-2c_1m}$ for every eigenvector $w\in\mathbb{F}_p^m$ of $\bar S_m$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$, so
$a_\beta(S_m)\le\frac1p+e^{-2c_1m}$ by~\eqref{eq:abetaeig}. Writing $R_p(S_m)$ for the number of repeated roots $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_p$ of
$\chi_{S_m}$ modulo $p$, we get, if $S_m\in\mathcal G_m$,
\[
N_{\Pi_n}(S_m)\le\sum_{n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}}\Big(\frac1p+e^{-2c_1m}\Big)R_p(S_m).
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:isocond}, applied to $S_m$ (valid as $23\le p\le e^{m^{1/9}}$), $\mathbb{E}(R_p(S_m))\le\frac{3.5}p+e^{-c_4m}$.
Hence, with $c':=\min(2c_1,c_4)$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}\big(N_{\Pi_n}(S_m);\ S_m\in\mathcal G_m\big)&\le\sum_{n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}}
\Big(\frac1p+e^{-2c_1m}\Big)\Big(\frac{3.5}p+e^{-c_4m}\Big)\\
&\le\sum_{k>n^{1/2-\varepsilon}}\frac{3.5}{k^2}+3e^{n^{1/10}-c'm},
\end{aligned}
\]
which tends to $0$, as $m\ge n-1$.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{prop:res2}
For all large $m$, on the event of Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue}, which has probability at least $1-e^{-m/200}$, the following holds
for every prime $23\le p\le e^{m^{1/8}}$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_{p^2}\setminus\mathbb{F}_p$ such that $\bar T-\lambda$ is invertible over
$\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. With $B:=(\bar T-\lambda)^{-1}$, we have $|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)/p)|\le e^{-c_2m/2}$ for all
$t\in\mathbb{F}_{p^2}^{\times}$, and $\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}B\xi=a)\le p^{-2}+e^{-c_2m/2}$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Let $t\ne0$. By~\eqref{eq:trres}, $C:=\operatorname{Tr}(tB)=P_t(\bar T)\beta(\bar T)^{-1}$, where $\beta$ is monic of degree $2$ with $\beta(\bar T)$
invertible and $P_t\ne0$ has degree at most $1$. Moreover $\xi^{\top}C\xi=\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)$ for $\xi\in\{\pm1\}^m$, as $\operatorname{Tr}$ is
$\mathbb{F}_p$-linear. So the first bound is the second claim of Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue}, for $Q=\beta$ and $P=P_t$. The additive characters
of $\mathbb{F}_q$ are $a\mapsto e^{2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(ta)/p}$, $t\in\mathbb{F}_q$ (Lidl--Niederreiter (1997)~\cite{LN97}), so by Fourier inversion over $\mathbb{F}_q$,
$\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}B\xi=a)\le q^{-1}+\max_{t\ne0}|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)/p)|$, and the second bound follows.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:SEd}
Let $d\in\{2,3,4\}$ and $c_5:=e^{-300}$. For all large $m$, with probability at least $1-e^{-m/9}$ the following holds for every prime
$p$ with $23\le p\le e^{m^{1/8}}$, and $p\ge m^{0.4}$ if $d\ge3$: for every monic irreducible $\beta\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree $d$ and every
nonzero $y\in\ker\beta(\bar T)$, $\mu(y)>c_5mp^2$. Consequently, on this event, for every such $p$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_{p^d}$ of
degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$, we have $\Pr_\xi(\bar\xi\perp K)\le p^{-dr}+e^{-2c_5m}$ for every subspace $K\subseteq\ker(\bar T-\lambda)$ over
$\mathbb{F}_{p^d}$ of dimension $r\ge1$.
In particular $\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}w=0)\le p^{-d}+e^{-2c_5m}$ for every eigenvector $w\in\mathbb{F}_{p^d}^m$ of $\bar T$ whose eigenvalue has degree
$d$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We fix the parameters and check the conditions of Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd}.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $G:=\mathbb{F}_p^d$, $N:=p^d$,
$\delta:=\frac1{100}$, and
\[
l:=\Big\lceil\frac{100d\log p}{\log m}\Big\rceil+50,\qquad s:=\lceil m^{0.6}\rceil,\qquad k:=\lceil m^{0.8}\rceil .
\]
For $d=2$ these are the parameters of the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:Ptrue}. For large $m$ the conditions of
Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd} hold uniformly in the primes $p$ of the statement, namely $l\ge50$, $s<k$, $s\ge16l\log(2N/\delta)$,
$s^{(l+1)/2}\ge32\delta^{-1}(1+\delta)\sqrt{\pi l}\,N(1.5l)^{2l}$, $s^{l/2}\ge100p^{d-1}(1.5l)^{2l}$, $s\ge1400l$ and, if $d\ge3$,
$p\ge\sqrt{s/l}$. Indeed, $1.5l\le m^{1/8}$ for large $m$, as $\log p\le m^{1/8}$, so $2l\log(1.5l)\le\frac14l\log m$ and
$s^{l/2}(1.5l)^{-2l}\ge m^{0.05l}\ge p^{5d}$, which exceeds $100p^{d-1}$ and $32\delta^{-1}(1+\delta)\sqrt{\pi l}\,Ns^{-1/2}$ (the latter
gives the condition on $s^{(l+1)/2}$). Moreover $s$ is much larger than $16l\log(200N)$ and $1400l$, and $\sqrt{s/l}\le m^{0.3}\le p$ if
$d\ge3$. Let $R^2:=c_5mp^2$ and $\sigma:=1/(2c_5p^2)$, so that $\sigma R^2=m/2$. Let $\theta_0$, $\mu_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss}
with $c=c_5$ (note $c_5\le10^{-5}$), and let $\nu^{\rm G}$ be the image on $\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ of the probability law proportional
to $e^{-\sigma z^2}$ on $\mathbb{Z}\setminus p\mathbb{Z}$, with largest atom $\nu^{\rm G}_{\max}$. So $\theta_0\le1.001$, $\mu_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_5}\,p$
and $\mu_0\nu^{\rm G}_{\max}\le1.001$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the event of Proposition~\ref{lem:suppd}, applied with $M=T$ and
$\{a,b\}=\{\pm1\}$, of probability at least $1-e^{-m/8}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We reduce the claim to linear systems for $T$ with fixed right sides.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $p$ and $\beta=x^d+\sum_{i<d}b_ix^i$ ($p^d$
choices). If $\mathcal S$ holds, $y\ne0$, $\beta(\bar T)y=0$ and $\mu(y)\le R^2$, a nonzero multiple of $y$, still in
$\ker\beta(\bar T)$, has an integer lift $z$ with $\|z\|^2\le R^2$. We call it $y$ again and put $Y:=(y,\bar Ty,\dots,\bar T^{d-1}y)$,
with rows $w_j\in G$. Then
\[
\bar TY=\Big(\bar Ty,\ \dots,\ \bar T^{d-1}y,\ -\sum_{i<d}b_i\bar T^iy\Big),
\]
a right side determined by $Y$, and $\lvert\operatorname{supp} y\rvert>m/(4(d+1))\ge m/20$ by Proposition~\ref{lem:suppd}.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3.}\ We sort the coordinates into classes and set up the weights.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces The classes are $Z$ ($w_j=0$), $D_2$ ($y_j\ne0$) and $D_4$
($y_j=0\ne w_j$). For each pattern $(D_2,D_4)$ with $|D_2|>m/20$ fix disjoint blocks of size $k$, $\lfloor|D_h|/k\rfloor$ of them
inside $D_h$ for $h=2,4$, depending only on the pattern. There is at least one, as $m/20\ge k$. Let $\rho^*(Y)$ be the smallest value
of $\rho_G$ on these blocks. The last statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:seqexp} (for vectors with entries in $G$), applied to a block
attaining $\rho^*(Y)$, bounds the probability over $T$ of the system of Step~2 by $\rho^*(Y)^{m-k}$, the right side being fixed.
We bound $\mathbf 1\{\|z\|^2\le R^2\}\le e^{\sigma(R^2-\|z\|^2)}$ and sum over all integer lifts $z$ of $y$. This gives a global factor
$e^{\sigma R^2}=e^{m/2}$. Let $G_0\le G$ be the hyperplane of the vectors with first coordinate $0$. The total weight of a class at one
coordinate (its \emph{mass}) and the normalized law $\nu_h$ of $w_j$ on $G\setminus\{0\}$ are as follows.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item $Z$: mass $\theta_0$.
\item $D_2$: mass $p^{d-1}\mu_0$, and $\nu_2:=\nu^{\rm G}\otimes(\text{uniform law on }\mathbb{F}_p^{d-1})$.
\item $D_4$: mass $(p^{d-1}-1)\theta_0$, and $\nu_4$ is uniform on $G_0\setminus\{0\}$.
\end{itemize}
So $\mathrm{mass}_h\,\nu_{h,\max}\le1.001$ for $h=2,4$, where $\nu_{h,\max}$ is the largest atom of $\nu_h$. A subspace $L\le G$ of
dimension $1\le g<d$ has $\nu_2(L)=p^{g-d}$ if $L\not\subseteq G_0$ (for each $\alpha\ne0$, the vectors of $L$ with first coordinate
$\alpha$ form an affine subspace of dimension $g-1$), and $\nu_2(L)=0$ if $L\subseteq G_0$, while $\nu_4(L)\le(p^g-1)/(p^{d-1}-1)$.
Hence, writing $\kappa_g(\nu)$ for the largest $\nu$-measure of a $g$-dimensional subspace, $\mathrm{mass}_2\,\kappa_g(\nu_2)=\mu_0p^{g-1}$
and $\mathrm{mass}_4\,\kappa_g(\nu_4)\le1.001p^g$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4.}\ We bound the contribution of the lowest level.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces The masses add up to $p^{d-1}(\theta_0+\mu_0)$. Summing over the $p^d$
polynomials $\beta$ and over the $Y$ with $\rho^*(Y)<(1+\delta)/N$, the contribution is at most
\[
p^de^{m/2}\big(p^{d-1}(\theta_0+\mu_0)\big)^m\Big(\frac{1+\delta}{p^d}\Big)^{m-k}
\le p^{d(k+1)}\Big(e^{1/2}(1+\delta)\Big(\frac{1.001}{23}+\sqrt{2\pi c_5}\Big)\Big)^m\le p^{d(k+1)}\,0.08^m .
\]

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 5.}\ We bound the contribution of the structured levels.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces For $a\ge0$ with $\rho_a:=2^a(1+\delta)/N\le1$, fix a pattern with
$|D_2|>m/20$, and consider the $Y$ with $\rho^*(Y)\in[\rho_a,2\rho_a)$. Every block then has $\hat\rho_G\ge\rho_G\ge\rho_a$, and under the
product of the laws $\nu_h$ the blocks are independent. By Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd}, a block of class $h$ has $\hat\rho_G\ge\rho_a$ with
probability at most $\zeta_h^{k-s}$, where $\zeta_h:=\gamma_{1,h}(\rho_a)+1.1\,\kappa_g(\nu_h)$ if $\rho_a$ lies in the window $W^{(g)}$ of
that proposition, $\zeta_h:=\gamma_{1,h}(\rho_a)$ if it lies in no window, and $\gamma_{1,h}$ is the function $\gamma_1$ of
Proposition~\ref{lem:blockd} for $\nu_h$. Let $M_h$ be $k-s$ times the number of blocks in $D_h$, and $M_{\rm bl}:=M_2+M_4$. As
$p^{-d}\le\rho_a\le1$ and $M_{\rm bl}\le m$, we have $(2\rho_a)^{m-k}\rho_a^{-M_{\rm bl}}\le2^mp^{dk}$. In each block, $k-s$ of the mass
factors are paired with one factor $\zeta_h$ of the block bound and with one factor $\rho_a$ (we call these coordinates the \emph{chain
coordinates}, and only their number matters). The at most $2k+s\lceil m/k\rceil\le4k$ remaining coordinates outside $Z$ have mass at most
$p^d$ each. So the contribution of the pattern and the level, summed over $\beta$, is at most
\[
p^de^{m/2}\,1.001^m\,p^{4dk}\cdot2^mp^{dk}\prod_{h=2,4}\big(\mathrm{mass}_h\,\zeta_h\,\rho_a\big)^{M_h}.
\]
Per chain coordinate,
$\mathrm{mass}_h\,\gamma_{1,h}(\rho_a)\rho_a=\mathrm{mass}_h\nu_{h,\max}\cdot64(1+\delta)\sqrt{\pi l}/(\delta\sqrt s)\le1.001\gamma_0$ with
$\gamma_0:=6464\sqrt{\pi l/s}$. If $\rho_a\in W^{(g)}$, then $\rho_a<1.1p^{-g}$, so that
$1.1\,\mathrm{mass}_2\kappa_g(\nu_2)\rho_a\le1.21\mu_0/p\le1.21\sqrt{2\pi c_5}$ and $1.1\,\mathrm{mass}_4\kappa_g(\nu_4)\rho_a\le1.22$.
Since $l=O(m^{1/8})$ uniformly in $p$ and $s\ge m^{0.6}$, we have $\gamma_0\to0$. Once $m$ is so large that
$\gamma_0\le\sqrt{2\pi c_5}$, every factor $\mathrm{mass}_h\zeta_h\rho_a$ is therefore at most $1.23$, and for $h=2$ at most
$1.001\gamma_0+1.21\sqrt{2\pi c_5}\le2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_5}$.
As $M_2\ge(k-s)(|D_2|/k-1)\ge m/21$, the product is at most $1.23^m(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_5})^{m/21}$. Finally $p^{5dk+d}=e^{O(m^{0.93})}$,
there are at most $3^m$ patterns and at most $d\log_2p+1$ levels, and $2\cdot1.001\,e^{1/2}\cdot3\cdot1.23<12.2$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 6.}\ We add the bounds of Steps~4 and~5, take a union bound over the primes, and deduce the bound for eigenvectors.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $\mathcal P_p$
be the probability that $\mathcal S$ holds and that some $\beta$ and $y$ as above exist for the prime $p$. By Steps~4 and~5, for large $m$,
\[
\mathcal P_p\le p^{d(k+1)}\,0.08^m+e^{o(m)}\,12.2^m\big(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_5}\big)^{m/21}\le e^{-m/2},
\]
since $2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_5}\le e^{-148}$ and so $12.2\,(2.42\sqrt{2\pi c_5})^{1/21}\le12.2\,e^{-7}<e^{-4.4}$. The union over the at most
$e^{m^{1/8}}$ primes and $\Pr(\mathcal S^c)\le e^{-m/8}$ show that the first claim fails with probability at most
$e^{m^{1/8}}e^{-m/2}+e^{-m/8}\le e^{-m/9}$.

For the consequence, let $q:=p^d$, let $\lambda$ and $K$ be as in the statement, and let $\beta$ be the minimal polynomial of $\lambda$.
For $\xi\in\{\pm1\}^m$ and $v\in\mathbb{F}_q^m$ we have $\operatorname{Tr}(\xi^{\top}v)=\sum_j\xi_j\operatorname{Tr}(v_j)$, and $v\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(\xi^{\top}v)$ is $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear.
As $K$ is a vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and the trace form of $\mathbb{F}_q$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is nondegenerate, $\bar\xi\perp K$ if and only if
$\operatorname{Tr}(\xi^{\top}v)=0$ for all $v\in K$. So Fourier inversion over the group $K$, which has $q^r$ elements, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_\xi\bigl(\bar\xi\perp K\bigr)&=\frac1{q^r}\sum_{v\in K}\prod_j\cos\frac{2\pi\operatorname{Tr}(v_j)}p
\le\frac1{q^r}+\max_{0\ne v\in K}\prod_j\Bigl|\cos\frac{2\pi\operatorname{Tr}(v_j)}p\Bigr|\\
&\le\frac1{q^r}+\max_{0\ne v\in K}e^{-2\mu(\operatorname{Tr}(v))/p^2},
\end{aligned}
\]
the last step by Lemma~\ref{lem:dilates}. For $0\ne v\in K$, $\operatorname{Tr}(v)$ is a nonzero vector of $\ker\beta(\bar T)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:simple}(a)), so $\mu(\operatorname{Tr}(v))>c_5mp^2$. The case of the line $K$ spanned by an eigenvector gives the last claim.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{thm:rank2}
There is an absolute constant $c_6>0$ such that for all large $n$, every prime $23\le p\le e^{n^{1/9}}$, $q=p^2$, and every
$\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\mathbb{F}_p$, a uniformly random Seidel matrix $S$ of order $n$ satisfies
\[
\Pr\bigl(\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S-\lambda I)\ge1\bigr)\le\frac1q+\frac{1.2}{q^2}+e^{-c_6n}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
We use the notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} with $d=2$, so that $L_m=\bar S_m-\lambda I$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and
$r_m=\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S_m-\lambda I)$. For $m_0\le m<n$ let $\mathcal E_m$ be the event that the conclusions of
Propositions~\ref{prop:Ptrue} and~\ref{prop:SEd} (with $d=2$) hold for $S_m$. For large $n$, $\Pr(\mathcal E_m^c)\le e^{-m/200}+e^{-m/9}$,
and these events cover $p$, as $e^{n^{1/9}}\le e^{m^{1/8}}$ for $m\ge m_0$. Put $\varpi:=e^{-c_2m_0/2}$, so that $\varpi\le10^{-5}$ for
large $n$, and $e^{-2c_5m}\le\varpi$ as $c_5>c_2$. We check the hypotheses (i) and (ii) of Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} on $\mathcal E_m$,
conditionally on $S_m$. If $r_m=0$, then by Lemma~\ref{lem:border}, with $B:=L_m^{-1}$, we have $r_{m+1}=1$ if and only if
$\xi^{\top}B\xi=-\lambda$. By Lemma~\ref{prop:res2} this has conditional probability at most $q^{-1}+e^{-c_2m/2}\le q^{-1}+\varpi$,
which is (i). If $r_m=r\ge1$, then $K_m=\ker L_m$ has dimension $r$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $\lambda$ has degree $2$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$, so
Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} (with $K=K_m$) gives $\Pr(\bar\xi\perp K_m)\le q^{-r}+e^{-2c_5m}\le q^{-r}+\varpi$, which is (ii).

So Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} applies, and moreover $\varpi=e^{-\Omega(n)}$, $n-m_0-2\ge n/4-3$ and
$\Pr(\mathcal E_{<n}^c)\le\sum_{m_0\le m<n}(e^{-m/200}+e^{-m/9})=e^{-\Omega(n)}$. As all these bounds are uniform in $p$ and $\lambda$, the
second claim of Lemma~\ref{lem:corank} gives the proposition for a suitable absolute constant $c_6>0$.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:deg2}
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)$. Then the probability that $E_p^{(2)}$ holds for some odd prime $p$ with
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ tends to $0$.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
Let $\Pi_n:=\{(p,2):\ p\text{ prime},\ n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}\}$, and for $m\in\{n-1,n\}$ let $\mathcal G_m$ be the event
that the conclusion of Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} with $d=2$ holds for $S_m$, so that $\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G_m)\le e^{-m/9}$ for large
$n$. We verify the remaining hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction}, which then proves the proposition. Let $n$ be large and
$m\in\{n-1,n\}$. Then every $(p,2)\in\Pi_n$ has $23<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}\le e^{m^{1/9}}$. Let $(p,2)\in\Pi_n$, $q=p^2$, and let
$\beta\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ be monic irreducible of degree $2$, with a root $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\mathbb{F}_p$. On $\mathcal G_m$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} and~\eqref{eq:abetaeig} give
\[
a_\beta(S_m)\le p^{-2}+e^{-2c_5m}.
\]
Let $f_p(S_m)$ be the number of monic irreducible quadratic factors of $\chi_{S_m}$ modulo $p$. Their roots are exactly the
$\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\mathbb{F}_p$ with $\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S_m-\lambda I)\ge1$, two for each factor. So by Proposition~\ref{thm:rank2}
(for the order $m$),
\[
\mathbb{E}(f_p(S_m))=\frac12\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\mathbb{F}_p}\Pr\bigl(\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S_m-\lambda I)\ge1\bigr)
\le\frac q2\Big(\frac1q+\frac{1.2}{q^2}+e^{-c_6m}\Big)\le1+\frac q2\,e^{-c_6m}.
\]
A repeated factor is in particular a factor, so $N_{\Pi_n}(S_m)\le\sum_pf_p(S_m)\,(p^{-2}+e^{-2c_5m})$ on $\mathcal G_m$, the sum running
over the primes $p\in(n^{1/2-\varepsilon},e^{n^{1/10}}]$. Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}\big(N_{\Pi_n}(S_m);\ S_m\in\mathcal G_m\big)&\le\sum_p\Big(1+\frac{p^2}2e^{-c_6m}\Big)\big(p^{-2}+e^{-2c_5m}\big)\\
&\le\sum_{p>n^{1/2-\varepsilon}}p^{-2}+\sum_{p\le e^{n^{1/10}}}\big(e^{-2c_5m}+p^2e^{-c_6m}\big).
\end{aligned}
\]
The first sum is at most $2n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$, and the second at most $e^{n^{1/10}-2c_5(n-1)}+e^{3n^{1/10}-c_6(n-1)}$. Both sums
tend to $0$, so the remaining hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction} holds.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:deg5}
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac1{10})$, and put
\[
\Pi_n^{\ge5}:=\{(p,d):\ p\text{ prime},\ n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}},\ 5\le d<3\log_2n\}.
\]
For $m\in\{n-1,n\}$ let $\mathcal G^{(5)}_m$ be the event that $\Delta_{S_m}\ne0$ and that the conclusion of
Proposition~\ref{lem:suppd} holds for $S_m$. Then $\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G^{(5)}_m)\to0$, and for large $n$ and $m\in\{n-1,n\}$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\big(N_{\Pi_n^{\ge5}}(S_m);\ S_m\in\mathcal G^{(5)}_m\big)\le96\,n^{-1/2+5\varepsilon}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{lem:simplespectrum}, $\Pr(\Delta_{S_m}=0)\to0$, and with Proposition~\ref{lem:suppd} this gives
$\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G^{(5)}_m)\to0$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We bound $a_\beta(S_m)$ with Lemma~\ref{lem:LObases}.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $n$ be large, $m\in\{n-1,n\}$, and suppose that
$S_m\in\mathcal G^{(5)}_m$. Let $n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$, let $\beta\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ be monic irreducible of degree $d$ with
$5\le d<3\log_2n$, and let $V$ be a simple $\bar S_m$-submodule of type $\beta$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:simple}(a), $V$ is a $d$-dimensional
subspace of $\ker\beta(\bar S_m)$. As $p\le e^{n^{1/10}}\le e^{m^{1/8}}$ and $d<3\log_2n\le m^{1/4}$, Proposition~\ref{lem:suppd} shows that
every nonzero vector of $V$ has more than $m/(4(d+1))$ nonzero coordinates. So Lemma~\ref{lem:LObases}(c) applies to $V$ with some
$k>m/(4(d+1))$ and $t=\lceil k/d\rceil\ge(n-1)/(4d(d+1))$. As $\lfloor t/2\rfloor\ge n/(74\log_2^2n)$ for $d<3\log_2n$ and large $n$
(in particular $t\ge2$), it gives
\[
\Pr_\xi(\bar\xi\perp V)\le\Big(\frac1p+\big(\pi\lfloor t/2\rfloor\big)^{-1/2}\Big)^d\le\Big(\frac1p+\frac{6\log_2n}{\sqrt
n}\Big)^d\le\big(2n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}\big)^d.
\]
This holds for every simple submodule of type $\beta$, hence for $a_\beta(S_m)$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We count the repeated factors and conclude the proof.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Since $\Delta_{S_m}\ne0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:budget}(b) with
$P=n^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ shows that there are at most $m^2\log(2m)/\log P\le3n^2$ pairs $(p,\beta)$ with $p>n^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $\beta$
a repeated factor of $S_m$ at $p$ (here $\varepsilon<\frac1{10}$ is used). For each of them that is counted in $N_{\Pi_n^{\ge5}}(S_m)$,
Step~1 gives $a_\beta(S_m)\le(2n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})^{\deg\beta}\le(2n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})^5$. So
$N_{\Pi_n^{\ge5}}(S_m)\le3n^2(2n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})^5=96\,n^{-1/2+5\varepsilon}$.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:fullsupp}
Fix $d\ge1$. For all large $m$, with probability at least $1-e^{-m^{1.05}}$, every odd prime $p\le m$ and every nonzero
$\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree $<d$ satisfy $\dim\ker\alpha(\bar T)\le(d-1)m^{0.55}$. For such $T$, every odd prime $p\le m$, every monic
$\beta\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ of degree $d$ with $\beta(\bar T)$ invertible, every $U\subseteq[m]$ with $|U|\ge0.4m$, and $u$ with support $U$ and
uniform signs on $U$,
\[
\Pr_u\Bigl(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(\alpha(\bar T)\beta(\bar T)^{-1}u)\rvert<\frac m{20}\ \text{for some nonzero }\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]\text{ of degree}<d\Bigr)
\ \le\ 2p^{d-1}\,2^{-0.06m}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
For the first statement, let $r_0:=\lceil m^{0.55}\rceil$, so that $r_0^2\ge m^{1.1}$ and $(d-1)(r_0-1)\le(d-1)m^{0.55}$. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:kernelpoly}, applied with $M=T$, $\{a,b\}=\{\pm1\}$ and $r=r_0$, and a union bound over the odd primes $p\le m$, the
first statement fails with probability at most $60\,m^d2^{-m^{1.1}/4}\le e^{-m^{1.05}}$.

For the second statement, fix a nonzero $\alpha$ of degree $<d$, which we may take monic (at most $2p^{d-1}$ choices). Put
$X:=\alpha(\bar T)\beta(\bar T)^{-1}$, and let $R\subseteq[m]$ with $|R^c|<m/20$. Then $\ker X=\beta(\bar T)\ker\alpha(\bar T)$, so the
columns of $X$ indexed by the set $U$ of the statement have rank at least $|U|-(d-1)m^{0.55}$, and
\[
\operatorname{rank} X_{R,U}\ge|U|-(d-1)m^{0.55}-m/20\ge0.35m-(d-1)m^{0.55}.
\]
By Odlyzko's lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:odlyzko}), applied to $u_U$, which is uniform on $\{\pm1\}^U$, we have
$\Pr_u((Xu)_R=0)\le2^{-\operatorname{rank} X_{R,U}}$, as $(Xu)_R=X_{R,U}u_U$. If $\lvert\operatorname{supp}(Xu)\rvert<m/20$, then $(Xu)_R=0$ for $R={[m]\setminus\operatorname{supp}(Xu)}$, one of
at most $2^{H(1/20)m}\le2^{0.287m}$ sets. A union bound over $\alpha$ and $R$ bounds the probability in the claim by
$2p^{d-1}2^{(0.287-0.35)m+(d-1)m^{0.55}}$, and as $0.287-0.35<-0.06$, the claim follows for large $m$.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:simple3}
Let $K\ge1$. There is $c_7=c_7(K)\in(0,c_5]$ such that for all large $m$, with probability at least $1-e^{-m/200}$, the
following holds for every prime $m^{0.4}\le p\le K\sqrt m$, with $q=p^3$, and every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of degree $3$ such that
$\bar T-\lambda$ is invertible: with $B:=(\bar T-\lambda)^{-1}$,
\[
\Pr_u\Bigl(\mu\big((\operatorname{Tr}(tB)u)_{U^c}\big)\le c_7mp^2\ \text{for some }t\in\mathbb{F}_q^{\times}\Bigr)\le e^{-m/100}.
\]
Hence $|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)/p)|\le e^{-c_7m/2}$ for $t\ne0$, and $\Pr_\xi(\xi^{\top}B\xi=a)\le q^{-1}+e^{-c_7m/2}$
for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_q$.
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
We first recall the trace identity, then fix the parameters of the union bound, and then prove the claim.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We recall the trace identity in degree three.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$ have degree $3$, with minimal polynomial
$\beta=x^3+b_2x^2+b_1x+b_0$. By the trace identity~\eqref{eq:trres} with $d=3$, if $\bar T-\lambda$ is invertible, then
$\operatorname{Tr}(t(\bar T-\lambda)^{-1})=P_t(\bar T)\beta(\bar T)^{-1}$ for $t\in\mathbb{F}_q$, where $t\mapsto P_t$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear bijection from $\mathbb{F}_q$
onto the polynomials of degree at most $2$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We fix the parameters of the union bound and specialize Lemma~\ref{lem:seqbases} to $d=3$.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $R^2:=cmp^2$ with $0<c\le c_5$ to
be chosen, and $\sigma:=1/(2cp^2)$, so that $\sigma R^2=m/2$. Let $\theta_0$, $\mu_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss} for this $c$ (note
$c\le c_5<10^{-5}$), so that $(\theta_0+\mu_0)/p\le1.001m^{-0.4}+\sqrt{2\pi c}$. We use Lemma~\ref{lem:seqbases} with
$d=3$, and write $t_0$ for its parameter $t$. Since $p\le K\sqrt m$, for large $m$ and $m/60\le t_0\le m/60+1$ we have
$\lfloor t_0/2\rfloor\ge m/121$, so that $p(\pi\lfloor t_0/2\rfloor)^{-1/2}\le6.21K$, and $1.6\cdot9\,p\sqrt{t_0}\le1.9Km$. For such $t_0$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:seqbases} gives, for the systems $\bar TW=Y$ below,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:seqb3}
\Pr(\bar TW=Y)\le p^{-3m}(1+6.21K)^{3m}e^{1.9Km}p^{18}.
\end{equation}

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 3.}\ We bound the probability of a short vector for fixed $p$, $\lambda$ and $u$, with $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Suppose that
$\bar T-\lambda$, hence also $\beta(\bar T)$, is invertible. Put $v:=\beta(\bar T)^{-1}u$ and $W:=(v,\bar Tv,\bar T^2v)$, with rows
$\varphi_j\in\mathbb{F}_p^3$, so that
\[
\bar TW=\big(\bar Tv,\ \bar T^2v,\ u-b_2\bar T^2v-b_1\bar Tv-b_0v\big)
\]
is determined by $(W,u)$, and $\operatorname{Tr}(tB)u=P_t(\bar T)v=\ell_t(W)$, where $\ell_t$ is the linear form on $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ given by the coefficients
of $P_t$, applied to each row of $W$. Nonzero multiples of $\operatorname{Tr}(tB)u$ are again of this form. Let $\mathcal E$ be the event that
$\lvert\operatorname{supp}\alpha(\bar T)v\rvert\ge m/20$ for every nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ with $\deg\alpha\le2$. As
$a^{\top}\varphi_j=((a_0+a_1\bar T+a_2\bar T^2)v)_j$, on $\mathcal E$ every hyperplane of $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ misses at least $m/20$ of the
$\varphi_j$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:seqbases} applies with $k=\lceil m/20\rceil$ and $t_0=\lceil k/3\rceil\in[m/60,m/60+1]$. Let
$\mathcal P(u)$ be the probability over $T$ that for some nonzero linear form $\ell$ on $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ and some $W$ with this property,
$\bar TW$ equals the right side above and $\ell(W)_{U^c}$ has an integer lift of squared norm at most $R^2$. As in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd}, we bound $\mathbf 1\{\|z\|^2\le R^2\}\le e^{\sigma(R^2-\|z\|^2)}$ and sum over the integer lifts $z$ of
$\ell(W)_{U^c}$. For each $\ell$, writing the rows of $W$ in coordinates on $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ whose last coordinate is $\ell$, the weighted number
of such $W$ is at most $e^{m/2}p^{3|U|}(p^2(\theta_0+\mu_0))^{|U^c|}$. With~\eqref{eq:seqb3} and $|U^c|\ge0.4m$ it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P(u)&\le p^3e^{m/2}p^{3m}\Big(\frac{\theta_0+\mu_0}p\Big)^{|U^c|}p^{-3m}(1+6.21K)^{3m}e^{1.9Km}p^{18}\\
&\le p^{21}\Big(e^{1/2}(1+6.21K)^3e^{1.9K}\big(1.001m^{-0.4}+\sqrt{2\pi c}\big)^{0.4}\Big)^m .
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose $c=c_7(K)\le c_5$ so small that $e^{1/2}(1+6.21K)^3e^{1.9K}(2\sqrt{2\pi c})^{0.4}\le e^{-2}$. For large $m$
we have $1.001m^{-0.4}\le\sqrt{2\pi c}$, and then $\mathcal P(u)\le p^{21}e^{-2m}\le(K\sqrt m)^{21}e^{-2m}\le e^{-m}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 4.}\ We average over $u$ and $T$, take a union bound over the pairs $(p,\lambda)$, and deduce the consequences.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $p$ and $\lambda$,
and let $\Phi(T)$ be the probability over $u$ of the event in the first claim if $\bar T-\lambda$ is invertible, and $\Phi(T):=0$
otherwise. As $|U|$ is the sum of the $m$ independent indicators $\mathbf 1\{u_j\ne0\}$ of mean $\frac12$, Hoeffding's inequality
(1963)~\cite[Theorem~2]{Hoe63} gives $\Pr\bigl(\big||U|-\frac m2\big|>0.1m\bigr)\le2e^{-m/50}$. As $u$ is independent of $T$,
$\mathbb{E}_T\Phi(T)$ is at most this bound, plus the failure probability $e^{-m^{1.05}}$ of the first part of Lemma~\ref{lem:fullsupp}, plus
$2p^2\,2^{-0.06m}$ for the complement of $\mathcal E$ (the second part of Lemma~\ref{lem:fullsupp} with $d=3$, as $p\le K\sqrt m\le m$),
plus the maximum of $\mathcal P(u)$ over the $u$ with $0.4m\le|U|\le0.6m$. So $\mathbb{E}_T\Phi(T)\le3e^{-m/50}$ for large $m$. By Markov's
inequality, $\Phi(T)>e^{-m/100}$ with probability at most $3e^{-m/100}$, and a union bound over the at most $K^4m^2$ pairs $(p,\lambda)$
shows that the first claim fails with probability at most $3K^4m^2e^{-m/100}\le e^{-m/200}$. For the consequences, let $t\in\mathbb{F}_q^{\times}$.
The last statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:squaring}, for the symmetric $\mathbb{F}_p$-matrix $C:=\operatorname{Tr}(tB)$, for which
$\xi^{\top}C\xi=\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)$, with $1$ in place of $t$ and with $c=c_7$, gives
$|\mathbb{E}_\xi\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(t\,\xi^{\top}B\xi)/p)|\le\sqrt2\,e^{-c_7m}\le e^{-c_7m/2}$ for large $m$. The last claim follows by Fourier
inversion over $\mathbb{F}_q$, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{prop:res2}.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:rank3}
Fix $K\ge1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac1{10})$. There is $c_8=c_8(K)>0$ such that for all large $n$, every prime
$p\in[n^{1/2-\varepsilon},K\sqrt n]$, $q=p^3$, and every $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of degree $3$, a uniformly random Seidel matrix $S$ of order
$n$ satisfies
\[
\Pr\bigl(\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S-\lambda I)\ge1\bigr)\le\frac1q+\frac{1.2}{q^2}+e^{-c_8n}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
We argue as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{thm:rank2}, with the following changes. Now $q=p^3$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$ has degree $3$, and for
$m_0\le m<n$ the event $\mathcal E_m$ is that the conclusions of Proposition~\ref{prop:simple3}, with $2K$ in place of $K$, and of
Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} with $d=3$ hold for $S_m$. For large $n$, $\Pr(\mathcal E_m^c)\le e^{-m/200}+e^{-m/9}$. These events cover
$p$: for $m\ge m_0$ we have $23\le m^{0.4}\le n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\le p\le K\sqrt n\le2K\sqrt m\le e^{m^{1/8}}$. In hypothesis (i) of
Lemma~\ref{lem:corank}, Proposition~\ref{prop:simple3} replaces Lemma~\ref{prop:res2}, and in hypothesis (ii), Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd}
is used with $d=3$ instead of $d=2$. Accordingly $\varpi:=e^{-c_7(2K)m_0/2}$, so that $\varpi\le10^{-5}$ for large $n$, and $\varpi$
bounds $e^{-c_7(2K)m/2}$ and $e^{-2c_5m}$ for $m\ge m_0$, as $c_7(2K)\le c_5$. The rest of the argument is unchanged, and it gives the
claim with a constant $c_8(K)>0$.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:deg34}
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac1{10})$, and let
\[
\Pi_n':=\{(p,d):\ p\text{ prime},\ n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}},\ d\in\{3,4\}\}.
\]
For $m\in\{n-1,n\}$ let $\mathcal G'_m$ be the event that the conclusion of Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} holds for $S_m$, for $d=3$ and
for $d=4$. Then, for large $n$, $\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G'_m)\le2e^{-m/9}$, and $\mathbb{E}(N_{\Pi_n'}(S_m);\ S_m\in\mathcal G'_m)\to0$ for
$m\in\{n-1,n\}$.
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
The bound on $\Pr(S_m\notin\mathcal G'_m)$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd}. Let $n$ be large, $m\in\{n-1,n\}$ and $(p,d)\in\Pi_n'$, so
that $23\le m^{0.4}\le n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}\le e^{m^{1/8}}$, and let $\beta$ be monic irreducible of degree $d$ over
$\mathbb{F}_p$. On $\mathcal G'_m$, Proposition~\ref{prop:SEd} and~\eqref{eq:abetaeig} give $a_\beta(S_m)\le p^{-d}+e^{-2c_5m}$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We treat degree four, and degree three at the primes $p>\sqrt n$, by counting factors.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces At each prime, at most $m/(2d)$ monic
irreducible $\beta$ of degree $d$ satisfy $\beta^2\mid\chi_{S_m}$ modulo $p$, as $\deg\chi_{S_m}=m$. By the elementary bound of
Chebyshev (1852)~\cite{Che52}, $\#\{p\le y\}\le2y/\log y$ for large $y$, so, splitting the primes $p>\sqrt n$ into the ranges $2^j\sqrt
n<p\le2^{j+1}\sqrt n$,
\[
\sum_{p>\sqrt n}p^{-3}\le\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{2^{j+3}\sqrt n}{\log n}\big(2^j\sqrt n\big)^{-3}=\frac{32}{3\,n\log n}.
\]
Hence, with the sums over the primes $p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$, these pairs contribute to $\mathbb{E}(N_{\Pi_n'}(S_m);\ S_m\in\mathcal G'_m)$ at most
\[
\sum_{p>n^{1/2-\varepsilon}}\frac n8\big(p^{-4}+e^{-2c_5m}\big)+\sum_{p>\sqrt n}\frac n6\big(p^{-3}+e^{-2c_5m}\big)
\le n^{-1/2+3\varepsilon}+\frac{16}{9\log n}+\frac n3\,e^{n^{1/10}-2c_5(n-1)},
\]
which tends to $0$.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We treat degree three at the primes $p\le\sqrt n$ with Proposition~\ref{thm:rank3}.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Here
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le\sqrt n$, so that $m^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le2\sqrt m$. Put $q:=p^3$, and let $f_p(S_m)$ be the number of monic
irreducible cubic factors of $\chi_{S_m}$ modulo $p$. Each of them has three roots $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of degree $3$, each with
$\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\bar S_m-\lambda I)\ge1$, and there are fewer than $q$ such $\lambda$. So Proposition~\ref{thm:rank3} with $K=2$, applied
to $S_m$, gives, with $c_8=c_8(2)$,
\[
\mathbb{E}(f_p(S_m))\le\frac q3\Big(\frac1q+\frac{1.2}{q^2}+e^{-c_8m}\Big)\le\frac12+\frac q3\,e^{-c_8m}.
\]
As a repeated factor is in particular a factor, these primes contribute at most
\[
\sum_{n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le\sqrt n}\Big(\frac12+\frac{p^3}3e^{-c_8m}\Big)\big(p^{-3}+e^{-2c_5m}\big)
\le n^{-1+2\varepsilon}+\sqrt n\big(e^{-2c_5(n-1)}+n^{3/2}e^{-c_8(n-1)}\big),
\]
which tends to $0$.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{thm:deg3plus}
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac1{10})$. Then the probability that $E_p^{(d)}$ holds for some odd prime $p$ with
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ and some $3\le d<3\log_2n$ tends to $0$.
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
The pairs $(p,d)$ in question lie in $\Pi_n^{\ge5}\cup\Pi_n'$, and for large $n$ all their primes are odd. By
Propositions~\ref{prop:deg5} and~\ref{prop:deg34}, the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction} hold for $\Pi_n^{\ge5}$ with the
events $\mathcal G^{(5)}_m$ (the bound $96\,n^{-1/2+5\varepsilon}$ tends to $0$, as $\varepsilon<\frac1{10}$) and for $\Pi_n'$ with the
events $\mathcal G'_m$. So for each of these two sets the probability that
$E_p^{(d)}$ holds for one of its pairs tends to $0$, and a union bound proves the proposition.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac1{10})$. The event of the theorem is the union of the events that $E_p^{(d)}$ holds for some odd prime $p$ with
$n^{1/2-\varepsilon}<p\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ and $d=1$, $d=2$, or some $3\le d<3\log_2n$, respectively. Their probabilities tend to $0$ by
Propositions~\ref{thm:deg1} and~\ref{thm:deg2}, which hold for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)$, and by Proposition~\ref{thm:deg3plus}.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:chebyshev}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $\vartheta(y)<y\log4$ for every real $y\ge1$.
\item $\sum_{p\le y}\frac{\log p}p<\log y+\log4$ for every real $y\ge2$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
(a) It suffices to show that $\prod_{p\le n}p<4^n$ for every integer $n\ge1$, and we argue by induction on $n$, following Erd\H{o}s. For
$n\le2$ the product is at most $2<4^n$. For even $n>2$ it follows from the case $n-1$, as $n$ is not prime. Let $n=2k+1\ge3$. Every prime
$p$ with $k+2\le p\le2k+1$ divides $\binom{2k+1}{k+1}=\frac{(2k+1)!}{(k+1)!\,k!}$, since it divides the numerator but not the denominator.
Moreover $2\binom{2k+1}{k+1}=\binom{2k+1}k+\binom{2k+1}{k+1}\le2^{2k+1}$, so $\binom{2k+1}{k+1}\le4^k$. With the case $k+1<n$ we get
$\prod_{p\le2k+1}p\le4^k\prod_{p\le k+1}p<4^k4^{k+1}=4^{2k+1}$. For real $y\ge1$ we then have
$\vartheta(y)=\vartheta(\lfloor y\rfloor)<\lfloor y\rfloor\log4\le y\log4$.

(b) Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. By Legendre's formula for the exponent of a prime in $n!$,
\[
\log n!=\sum_{p\le n}\log p\sum_{k\ge1}\Big\lfloor\frac n{p^k}\Big\rfloor\ \ge\ \sum_{p\le n}\Big\lfloor\frac np\Big\rfloor\log p\
>\ \sum_{p\le n}\Big(\frac np-1\Big)\log p=n\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}p-\vartheta(n).
\]
Since $\log n!\le n\log n$, part~(a) gives $\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}p<\log n+\frac{\vartheta(n)}n<\log n+\log4$. For real $y\ge2$ we
apply this with $n:=\lfloor y\rfloor$.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{lem:valuations}
Let $g\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ be monic of degree $j\ge1$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer such that $g(a)\ne0$ for $a=1,\dots,N$, and let
$X\ge\max_{1\le a\le N}|g(a)|$. Then for every prime $p$,
\[
\sum_{a=1}^Nv_p\big(g(a)\big)\ \le\ j\Big(\frac N{p-1}+\frac{\log X}{\log p}+1\Big).
\]
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 1.}\ We factor $g$ over a $p$-adic field.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Let $L$ be a splitting field of $g$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. It is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, so
$v_p$ extends uniquely to a valuation $v:L\to\mathbb{Q}\cup\{\infty\}$ with $v(p)=1$, which satisfies $v(yy')=v(y)+v(y')$ and
$v(y+y')\ge\min(v(y),v(y'))$. Write $g=\prod_{i=1}^j(x-\gamma_i)$ with $\gamma_i\in L$. Every root satisfies $v(\gamma_i)\ge0$. Indeed, let
$\gamma$ be a root with $v(\gamma)<0$, and write $g=x^j+\sum_{k<j}b_kx^k$ with $b_k\in\mathbb{Z}$. In the identity $\gamma^j=-\sum_{k<j}b_k\gamma^k$
the left side has valuation $jv(\gamma)$, while every term on the right side has valuation $v(b_k)+kv(\gamma)\ge kv(\gamma)>jv(\gamma)$,
which is impossible. Hence $v(a-\gamma_i)\ge\min(v(a),v(\gamma_i))\ge0$ for every integer $a$ and every $i$, and
\[
v_p\big(g(a)\big)=\sum_{i=1}^jv(a-\gamma_i).
\]

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Step 2.}\ We bound the contribution of one root.\par\nobreak\noindent\ignorespaces Fix $i$ and put $\tau:=\log X/\log p$. For $1\le a\le N$ all the terms $v(a-\gamma_{i'})$
are nonnegative, so $v(a-\gamma_i)\le v_p(g(a))\le\tau$, because $p^{v_p(g(a))}$ divides the nonzero integer $g(a)$, whose absolute value is
at most $X$. For real $t>0$ let $C(t)$ be the number of $a\in\{1,\dots,N\}$ with $v(a-\gamma_i)\ge t$, so that $C(t)=0$ for $t>\tau$. If $a$
and $a'$ are two of them, then $v_p(a-a')=v\big((a-\gamma_i)-(a'-\gamma_i)\big)\ge t$, and since $v_p(a-a')$ is an integer or $\infty$,
